task.title: Background repetition and attachment
task.shortdesc: These CSS properties specify whether a background image repeats to fill its area and what the image is attached to.

info.p: “CSS Backgrounds 4 §2.4, Tiling Images Shorthand: the background-repeat property”.

Use background-repeat to specify whether an image repeats horizontally, vertically, both or neither. One value applies to both axes. Two values set the horizontal and vertical behavior, in that order.

Use repeat to tile the image, no-repeat to show it once, space to distribute whole copies with space between them, or round to resize the copies so they fit evenly. repeat-x and repeat-y repeat on one physical axis only. repeat-block and repeat-inline repeat on the logical block or inline axis, respectively, and do not repeat on the other axis. Separate values for multiple image layers with commas.
CSSMedia expands background-repeat into its physical or logical axis properties.
“CSS Backgrounds 4 §2.3, Tiling Images: the background-repeat-x, background-repeat-y, background-repeat-block, and background-repeat-inline properties”.

Use these properties to specify repetition on one axis. The x and y properties use the physical horizontal and vertical axes. The inline and block properties use the logical axes, which follow the element’s writing mode.
Each accepts repeat, no-repeat, space or round. Use the shorthand when you want to set both axes together.
“CSS Backgrounds 4 §2.5, Affixing Images: the background-attachment property”.

Use background-attachment to specify how a background image is positioned in relation to its box or its contents. In paged media, CSS defines fixed relative to the page box, so that the background is repeated on each page.
In paged media, fixed attaches the image to the page box. The initial value is scroll, which attaches the image to the box. Separate values for multiple image layers with commas.
